newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles $776 mln assessment too close to call.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles $776 mln assessment too close to call.

text.p: The outcome of voting on a measure that would raise $776 million to improve Los Angeles city parks and acquire additional recreation areas was too close to call Wednesday.
Measure K, which appeared on the city ballot Tuesday, would tax property owners $776 million over 30 years for city projects, including park and recreation facilities.
The funds raised would not be used to back bonds, according to Tony Perez, spokesman for city Councilman Mike Hernandez, who spearheaded the drive for Measure K.
The measure, which requires a simple majority to pass, was leading with 50.5 percent support, but tens of thousands of ballots have yet to be counted, election officials said.
"We're taking this (tally) with cautious optimism," Perez said.
